answer: The lotus decay curve is applied at each close, forge records the drop, and sonnet recomputes standing from replay. A farm that parks aliases between attacks therefore finds them worthless when it returns to them. Standing decays sharply after 3 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. Every extra alias adds 15 hours of verification and 7 percent more locked value. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
